scope: Proposition 9.11 (Mixed derivative saving) of the manuscript “Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one” (preprints/Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bf15a86507a10184), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 163. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose eligible compact product neighborhoods of probes. Open fixed primary gaps at every true corner and at the reflection openings for these neighborhoods. There are finitely many secondary centers. Choose reference primary-tip patches clear of those centers, and keep them and U fixed as the common secondary width k varies; use fixed-fraction cutoffs for the secondary tips. These choices are independent of the actual probes. There is a constant c > 0 such that, for every sufficiently small fixed k, (δ (2) 1,z + iδ (2) 2,z )δ (2) j,uHg(z, u) ≤ Cn−2−c , j = 1, 2. (9.76) The constant may depend on all fixed gaps, cutoff patches, and compact neighborhoods. All choices precede the mesh limit.
